frozen_decisions_applied: Plan S5 #18: 'Add a dedicated protected reset-journal storage port that survives erasing user/application namespaces and can atomically represent the four FD-21 states.' -- both halves implemented directly: 'survives erasing' via kResetJournal's RESET_JOURNAL_ONLY classification (Section 2.7) plus Section 2.13's erase_namespace() structural refusal (proven by a dedicated cross-module test, not just asserted); 'atomically represent' via a single u32 key written in one hal_nvs_set_u32 call, inheriting atomicity from ESP-IDF's own NVS commit semantics rather than reimplementing it.

FD-21's exact four states (requested -> erasing -> reinitialized -> commissioning_ready), already defined as ResetJournalState in Section 2.7's registry header (added proactively in that earlier sub-slice specifically so this one could reference the real names now), are used directly -- no redefinition or renaming.

Plan FD-22 ('Prefer ESP-IDF-provided ... platform lifecycle mechanisms ... over duplicating a platform state machine') was applied directly: this port does not implement its own atomicity/commit logic, it relies entirely on NVS's own single-key-write guarantee.

registry_extended.detail: kResetJournal gained one key pattern ('reset_journal', exact) and implemented_today flipped from false to true, consistent with the registry's own stated bar for that flag (real hal_nvs_* call sites exist).

storage_port_implemented.detail: get_reset_journal_state(ResetJournalState*) reuses SecureStorageStatus directly (kNotProvisioned/kAvailable/kCorrupt/kUnavailable) rather than inventing a parallel vocabulary; a raw stored value outside the four valid enum values is explicitly classified kCorrupt (verified with a direct test that writes an out-of-range raw u32 via hal_nvs_set_u32 and confirms the port catches it). set_reset_journal_state(ResetJournalState) validates the input is one of the four defined states before writing anything (kRejectedInvalidState otherwise) and has no encryption-gate dependency since kResetJournal has encryption_required==false (a small state enum, not secret material).
